sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Transgenic males carrying hPRSS55-3xFLAG-GPI on a Prss55-null background sired offspring, demonstrating full fertility rescue and confirming functional surface expression of the tagged protein.
sites.rationale: PRSS55 is a GPI-anchored serine protease; the entire region 19–352 is extracellular per the computed topology. The hPRSS55-3xFLAG-GPI construct places the 3xFLAG between the mature protein body and the GPI anchor signal sequence, so after GPI attachment and C-terminal signal cleavage the tag is displayed on the extracellular face. No specific residue junction is named in the ledger, so insert_after_residue is null and the position is topology_derived. Fertility rescue in Prss55-null mice confirms both surface display and full biological function of the tagged construct. Full-length human PRSS55 (NM_198464.4) with a C-terminal 3xFLAG tag inserted prior to the native GPI anchor signal sequence (hPRSS55-3xFLAG-GPI construct), expressed in transgenic mice on a Prss55-null background. The GPI signal is retained downstream of the tag, so after GPI attachment and signal cleavage the 3xFLAG is left at the extracellular C-terminus of the mature, membrane-anchored protein. No specific residue number is named for the tag junction in the ledger; the C-terminal extracellular position is derived from the stated topology of the construct.

sources.claim: The first construct, designated hPRSS55-3xFLAG-GPI , was engineered to retain the native glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI) anchor signal sequence, thereby positioning the 3xFLAG tag extracellularly.

literature_notes: Three additional C-terminal tag constructs were considered but classified as intracellular and placed in other_positions. (1) hPRSS55-TM-3xFLAG (L3): the native GPI signal is replaced by a transmembrane domain followed by 3xFLAG; the paper explicitly states the tag is intracellular. (2) Mouse Prss55-EGFP via pEGFP-N2 (L6/L7): full-length cDNA including the GPI signal is cloned upstream of EGFP, so EGFP is appended after the GPI signal sequence. When a hydrophobic GPI signal is followed by a large globular domain, the signal is not cleaved but instead acts as a single-pass TM anchor, placing EGFP on the cytoplasmic face; L7 shows membrane-localised EGFP consistent with this topology, not extracellular display. (3) proT-SP1/1-EGFP (L8/L9, PMID 18844450): same architecture — full-length C-terminal EGFP on a GPI protein — and L9 shows the fusion in the membrane fraction, again consistent with intracellular EGFP. None of these three constructs qualify as extracellular surface tag sites. No ledger line names a specific residue for any tag junction in PRSS55, so the one qualifying site is region-level (insert_after_residue null).

literature_other_positions.note: hPRSS55-TM-3xFLAG: GPI anchor signal replaced by a transmembrane domain; 3xFLAG follows the TM domain and is explicitly stated to be intracellular.

Mouse Prss55-EGFP (pEGFP-N2, full-length cDNA): EGFP is appended after the GPI signal sequence; the hydrophobic GPI signal likely acts as a TM anchor, placing EGFP on the cytoplasmic face; membrane localisation confirmed in HEK293 cells (L7).

proT-SP1/1-EGFP (PMID 18844450, full-length C-terminal EGFP): protein found mainly in the membrane fraction of HEK293 cells (L9), consistent with intracellular EGFP anchored via the GPI signal acting as a TM domain.
